transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
Since my husband’s heart attack, it’s like I’m not really here. When I walk into his hospital room, everything feels unreal, like I’m watching it happen to someone else.
I am so sorry you are going through this. To help me understand better, when did your husband's heart attack happen, and how long have you been feeling this way?
My husband's heart attack happened six days ago at our home. I have been feeling this strange, disconnected way ever since that very afternoon.
Besides this feeling of unreality, have you been experiencing other symptoms like intense anxiety, sadness, trouble sleeping, or difficulty coping with daily tasks?

Yes, I can't seem to manage daily tasks—I've skipped my own doctor appointments and stopped going to my quilting circle because even paying bills or cooking feels like too much. I also feel completely blank inside when friends try to comfort me, and I find myself snapping at my daughter and jumping out of my skin at every little noise.
Are you also experiencing sudden, unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the moment your husband had his heart attack?

Yes, I keep seeing his face turning that awful blue and hearing that gurgling sound pop into my head out of nowhere, even when I'm just washing dishes or trying to read. It feels like I'm right back there in that moment, with my hands slipping on his chest all over again.
Are you finding yourself actively trying to avoid thoughts, feelings, or physical reminders—like the room where it happened—that bring back memories of his heart attack?

Yes, I won’t let myself think about that afternoon at all. I even take the long way around the hospital so I don’t have to walk past the ER doors, because just catching a glimpse of the ambulances makes my stomach flip and makes me feel like I might completely fall apart.
Have you noticed these intense feelings and reactions starting to ease up at all over the last few days, or have they remained just as strong?
No, they haven't eased up at all, and it feels just as intense and overwhelming as it did that first day. I am so exhausted, but there has been absolutely no relief since he collapsed six days ago.
Have you ever experienced any other highly traumatic or life-threatening events in the past, and did you have similar symptoms that lasted for more than a month after those events?
No, I've never experienced anything this traumatic in my entire life. I have never had symptoms like this in the past, so this is all completely new and terrifying to me.
Before your husband's heart attack, did you have any history of mental health conditions, such as anxiety or depression?
No, I’ve never had any issues with anxiety, depression, or any other mental health conditions before this happened. I've always been a very active, social person, so this is all completely new to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient experienced a severe traumatic event (witnessing her husband's life-threatening heart attack) 6 days ago and developed immediate, severe symptoms of intrusion, avoidance, dissociation (derealization, depersonalization, emotional numbing), and hyperarousal. Because the symptoms have lasted for only 6 days, they do not meet the duration criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1), which typically requires symptoms to persist for at least 1 month. Therefore, Acute Stress Reaction (F43.0) is the most appropriate diagnosis.
